label: Belief and practice
quiz: Which statement separates practice from private belief?
A recorded action does not reveal every participant's inner understanding
Every public action proves identical belief
An institution contains every person's thoughts
A ceremony erased all earlier traditions
retry: What should a learner ask after finding a ceremony record?
What event is recorded and what further evidence supports claims about people's understanding?
Why must everyone everywhere have believed identically?
Which prayer must the student perform?
Why is every private motive now certain?
hard: A caption turns one recorded event into universal conversion. What revision fits?
Keep the event and identify the unsupported claim about all people
Erase the event solely because the broad claim is unsupported
Treat missing evidence as proof of agreement
Assess the student's religion instead of the source

label: Community spaces
quiz: What does Silang's 1595 parish establishment date establish most directly?
A dated institutional development, not the age of every later building feature
Every feature visible today was built in 1595
Every resident used the place identically
A complete record of every private belief
retry: Why compare a parish record with construction evidence?
Institutional beginnings and a building's development can concern different dates
All visible features must have one date
A photograph supplies all earlier uses
A parish name proves universal participation
hard: An early parish date and a later photograph are supplied. What still needs checking?
When the pictured features were built and how the place was used
Only a larger copy of the photograph
Why every resident necessarily approved
Which invented date can fill every gap

label: Art and makers
quiz: What does a commissioned religious object help investigate?
Making, context, patronage and use
Every maker's exact private motive
The belief of every viewer
The absence of earlier local skills
retry: Why keep artisans visible in an account of religious art?
Objects involved people and existing skills rather than appearing without makers
Local creativity began only when outsiders arrived
A patron performed every task alone
All makers had one identical reason
hard: A church commission is recorded but no maker testimony is supplied. Which claim needs separate evidence?
The maker's exact personal belief and motive
That a commission appears in the record
That the object has a documented purpose
That making and use can be studied

label: Continuity and change
quiz: Which statement correctly treats continuity?
Something can carry on while other practices or institutions change
Every older practice necessarily disappeared
All communities followed one identical combination
Modern practice proves every earlier detail
retry: What does local interpretation emphasize?
People helped shape how messages were understood in particular settings
Everyone received every message identically
Local participants had no knowledge
A text alone reveals all reception
hard: A fictional case records a new observance and an older custom continuing. What is careful?
Describe both actions and investigate their meanings without assigning one belief to all
Declare every community combined beliefs identically
Treat the two actions as proof of all private motives
Erase one action because both cannot occur

label: Dated heritage evidence
quiz: What does a present-day heritage exhibition fail to establish alone?
That all displayed details existed unchanged in the colonial period
That the exhibition describes a tradition
That heritage can be studied respectfully
That objects and practices can matter to communities
retry: How should a learner use the Moryonan example?
As a named living heritage example while checking dated evidence for earlier features
As proof that all costumes never changed
As a requirement to perform penitential practices
As the history of every religious community
hard: A modern costume is shown beside an older text naming only an event. What should be checked?
Which details each dated source actually supports
Why every modern feature must be ancient
Which invented eyewitness speech confirms all details
Why source dates should be ignored
